observations.contract: Historical panel identity and connected source
observations.trace: PatternSpec retains named panels and StitchSide panel strings; stitched_segments builds a name-to-index map and build_garment converts names into ordinal SeamSide references and preserves panel names in cloth Panel. Original delegate746 had read2266 fully and later independently read registered connected ranges of PatternSpec and cloth; original root adoption recorded zero personal rereads and no ordered-source credit.
observations.remaining: Original316 already identified string propagation, duplicate/merge and missing reference policies as open. The exact historical connected receipt and registrations are retained with their original6533 attribution; new95e bounded source views do not grant full future role2629 or2631 credit.

observations.trace: PatternSpec.panels is a public Vec and PatternSpec.panel finds the first matching name. build_garment inserts each retained name into panel_index, so a later usable duplicate replaces an earlier value. Thus for a symbolic input with two usable panels named the same, PatternSpec.panel selects the first while a stitch lookup in the fitter selects the last.
observations.remaining: Original connected reviewer already raised duplicate-name policy. The first-versus-last distinction is a current source comparison, conditional on duplicates surviving admission; no pattern or mesh ran. Whether duplicates should be rejected, merged or otherwise resolved and exact aliases remain open.

observations.trace: Both stitched_segments and build_garment continue past a stitch whose named panel is absent or whose edge index is outside its panel. build_garment separately records panels with too-short outlines in skipped, but it does not record a missing stitch reference there. The selected creator explicitly rejects nonempty skipped panels or empty mesh after build.
observations.remaining: Original316 already identified missing-reference and skipped-panel policy as unresolved. A valid usable panel plus a stitch naming a nonexistent panel is a conditional malformed PatternSpec case; whether the library must reject or report it and exact consumers remain open. No pattern, mesher or creator ran.

observations.trace: EdgeSpec exposes endpoint indices and Curvature quadratic/cubic parameter Vecs. The fit samples panel edges through edge_as_curve, which directly indexes both vertices and the required one or two control points. A symbolic public edge with an out-of-bounds endpoint, or a quadratic with an empty params Vec, reaches distinct direct index operations rather than the fallible build_garment boundary returning an error.
observations.remaining: Malformed PatternSpec values and supported external producer/schema policies are not established. The endpoint and control-point failures are distinct first operations; no pattern, index, curve or panic ran. Other native pattern consumers and aliases remain open.

observations.trace: PatternSpec.properties publicly stores units_in_meter with default100 and serializes that field. build_garment unconditionally multiplies panel coordinates and translations by CM_TO_M=0.01; its documented input is centimetres. A symbolic PatternSpec whose numeric coordinates are in metres and units_in_meter=1 would therefore be interpreted as centimetres by this adapter.
observations.remaining: No producer is shown to supply non-centimetre patterns, and the contract may intentionally restrict fitting to centimetres. Whether non-100 declarations should be rejected or honored, and whether a single canonical unit owner exists, remain open. No pattern or mesh ran.

observations.trace: Fit.clear_body says it lifts every inside particle and describes a host query as not radius-limited, but passes reach=0.5 metres to TriangleBvh.closest_point. The BVH traversal squares that limit and returns only candidates within it. If a hypothetical interior particle is more than0.5m from every triangle, the query returns None and the loop continues without lifting it.
observations.remaining: This is a source-level conditional contradiction with the broad comment, not an observed fit failure; realistic wearer extent and desired maximum clearance are unestablished. No particle, triangle query, BVH or GPU ran.

observations.trace: Fit.set_body installs the supplied surface both as GPU collision mesh and retained host body before clear_body. The selected creator may subsequently call set_collision_mesh with a combined body-and-obstacle surface, updating the GPU collision mesh without updating the retained host body; Fit.reset later uses the host body for clear_body.
observations.remaining: The split may be intentional because clear_body names the wearer rather than every obstacle. No assumed error or ordinary scenario is claimed. Required reset/obstacle clearance authority, other callers and native synchronization remain open.

observations.trace: Fit.set_pose calls particles.write_positions; that delegates to Particles.write, which uploads both current and previous positions and at-rest velocities. The source therefore supports the stated rest reset on the successful path.
observations.remaining: No write, pose, solver or runtime ran. Partial device-write errors and all other pose behavior were not assessed by this rejection.
